task: round 15 skeptic (VALUE+FEASIBILITY) of R15DS-3 SHIFT(-0.05) hypothesis weights for the probe 43/44 read
reason: Feasibility is fine. This is a reading hypothesis: nothing is built, R8 is not touched and no slot is used. VALUE fails as stated, for four reasons. (1) The weight ~0.5 is unearned. The -0.05 shift was fitted after the fact to the one 0.30 read, and that read only says that ~2-3 public TPs sit in [0.25,0.30). The only extra support for 'nothing below 0.25' is the sjlee forks (CONTEXT l.698-710), which run on a different 0.947 stack: no x138 linker, no DaughterNet, a different set of orphan candidates (v_plancheck_pc15-03 notes l.5 says the same). They are also 3-dp ties. The 0.20 vs 0.25 tie means an unrounded |d| < 0.001, and 1 TP + 2 FP in the band at the scanner's own public per-event values (+0.0023/-0.0007) gives +0.0009, which still displays as a tie. The 0.15 vs 0.20 reading (0.946 vs 0.947) fits either an FP-only band or 1 TP + ~4 FP. So these ties barely discriminate SHIFT from BROAD-lite or DECAY. (2) SHIFT and LAB-like/NOISE predict the same thing for 43/44: the bands below 0.25 are FP-only, so both give 0.953/0.954. Splitting 0.5 vs 0.15 between them changes no row of R1-R5, and neither R3 nor R4 can confirm SHIFT. The only decision-relevant split is NARROW (TPs confined to >= 0.25, i.e. SHIFT + LAB, about 0.6-0.65) against BROAD/DECAY. (3) Attribution: the scanner treats the -0.005 as division TPs only and prices edges at ~4e-5 per lost TP fork. But the exp60 lab (experiments/exp60_trainlab/results.md) shows a real edge/node channel on 44b6: at dc0.30, adj edge -0.0012 with nodes -49 and 0 TP lost; at dc0.35, edge -0.0022 with nodes -88. 6bba shows about +0.0002. Part of the public -0.005 may be edge loss from dropped daughter nodes, not a shifted TP cluster. The lab dc arms also ran without the insertion, while public exp70d had it. The exp70d ledger rules out a runtime artefact (L (7.19,7.36] h; the insertion gate did not fire). (4) The private clause 'a DC variant can beat K2 on private only if R1/R2 refute SHIFT' is a non sequitur. The private embryos are other embryos. A public R1/R2 is neither necessary nor sufficient for a private gain: lab 6bba says dc0.20 = -0.0008 (+6 FP, 0 TP), and a private embryo could be shifted independently of public. The robust statement is simply that DC variants stay class C and K2 0.25 stays in the finals, which R15DS-6 and L9 already say. Net: the reading rows stand, but the hypothesis label and weight should not be written into CONTEXT as the leading explanation.
fix: In the 43/44 pre-registration, keep R1-R5 and their numeric priors unchanged. Replace the four-way weights with two decision-relevant classes: NARROW (the public TP cluster is confined to >= 0.25; SHIFT or LAB, which 43/44 cannot tell apart) ~0.6, and BROAD/DECAY (TPs continue below 0.25) ~0.4. Label SHIFT(-0.05) 'post-hoc, one free parameter, not testable by 43/44'. Add one caveat line: part of the dc0.30 cost may be the edge/node channel (lab 44b6: dc0.30 edge -0.0012, nodes -49), so 'k TPs lost' is an upper bound. Drop the private sentence. Replace it with: 'DC variants remain class C; a public R1/R2 is necessary but not sufficient for any finals ask (6bba lab dc0.20 = -0.0008).' No build, no slot, no rule change.
realistic_gain: 0 on private and public: nothing is submitted or changed. The only value is cleaner reading hygiene. It avoids overweighting a post-hoc embryo-shift story when the private-read and finals asks are written (the R15DS-6 coin flip stays a coin flip).
